verdict.rationale: Devin's first-party docs say users can connect external MCP tool servers to Devin CLI. Those tools give the agent access to APIs, databases and other services, fall under the same permission system as built-in tools, and are exposed as slash commands. The docs also describe MCP integrations such as Datadog, Sentry and Figma for Devin generally. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration, and detailed setup and transport documentation in the evidence (e.g., how servers are registered and whether stdio or HTTP is supported).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can plug MCP servers into this product so it can use their tools

citations.quote: MCP (Model Context Protocol) lets you connect external tool servers to Devin CLI, giving the agent access to APIs, databases, issue trackers, and any other service you can wrap in an MCP server.
MCP tools are subject to the same permission system as built-in tools.
Devin CLI exposes each one as a slash command
Extend Devin's reach with MCP integrations: Connect Devin to Datadog, Sentry, databases, Figma, Notion, Stripe, and hundreds of other tool
